_note: W-001's oracle (tests/window/WindowCases.ps1, Get-OracleRow), row by row: the shapes a panel row can have once its scan is over, bounded by who produces them, and the class the oracle must give each (SL-089 criterion 3, review m3: oracle rows whose cause changed between the scan and the check). Core.Tests' W001OracleTests builds each plant for real in a temp tree, part of it before the moment it takes as the scan's start and part after, and feeds the rows to the script's own function. plant is what the row's folder is when the oracle looks: denied (this user denied listing it, as when the scan ran), listable (made before the scan, untouched since), acl-reset (denied before the scan, the deny taken away after it), recreated (deleted after the scan and made again), gone (deleted after the scan), junction (a reparse point, made before the scan), held (listable, and held open without read sharing from before the scan until the oracle has run), held-acl-reset (denied before the scan, the deny taken away after it, and held from then on). Rows F17 and F18 (SL-003) are the class refused-another-code and its exemption. preM3 is what the oracle as first designed gave the same row: it opened every NothingListed row but 363 and reparse points and exempted only code-2 folders made after the scan, so every row whose cause had ended read as a leak and failed a correct run. Rows F03, F04, F06, F07, F09 and F10 are the ones review m3 closes. Row F16 (SL-106) is the third kind: a code-5 row whose folder lists now, as an SMB server that refuses the first page after CREATE leaves it, is a folder that opened, so it is tallied and never opened and never a leak; before SL-106 the oracle had no class for the kind and gave unknown-kind.
